name: Enneagram Test
tagline: Discover the core motivation behind how you think and act.
intro: The Enneagram describes nine personality types, each driven by a different core motivation and core fear. This test measures how strongly you identify with each of the nine patterns and highlights the one that fits you best. Rate 100 short statements; it takes about five minutes.
seoDescription: Which of the nine Enneagram types are you? Take this free 5-minute test, see your scores on all nine types and get growth tips for your main type.

type1.name: Type 1: The Perfectionist
type1.short: Driven by the wish to be good, correct and to improve the world; fears being wrong or flawed.
type1.low: The Perfectionist pattern plays only a small role for you. You are relaxed about rules and mistakes and do not feel a strong inner critic pushing you to get everything right. This lets you go with the flow and forgive easily. Tip: in areas where quality really matters, such as health or finances, a little more structure and attention to detail may serve you. Check whether easy-going sometimes means letting important standards slip.
type1.mid: You recognise some Perfectionist traits. You care about doing things properly and can be self-critical, but you also know when good enough is fine. Your sense of right and wrong guides you without dominating you. Tip: notice when your inner critic gets louder, often under stress, and answer it kindly. Choose consciously where high standards add value and where flexibility makes life easier.
type1.high: The Perfectionist pattern is strong in you. You are principled, conscientious and driven to improve yourself and the world. Your core fear is being wrong, bad or flawed, so a strict inner critic often keeps you in line. You bring integrity and quality to everything you do. Tip: practise accepting imperfection, both in yourself and others; mistakes are part of learning. Allow yourself pleasure and play without first earning it. Growth comes when you trust that you are already good enough.

type2.name: Type 2: The Helper
type2.short: Driven by the wish to be loved and needed; fears being unwanted or unworthy of love.
type2.low: The Helper pattern plays a minor role for you. You do not build your identity around being needed and are comfortable focusing on your own life. This protects you from over-giving. Tip: make sure the people close to you still feel your care; small gestures, such as checking in or offering help unasked, keep relationships warm. Notice when independence turns into distance.
type2.mid: You recognise some Helper traits. You enjoy supporting others and like being appreciated, but you can also put yourself first when needed. Your warmth is balanced with self-respect. Tip: notice whether you sometimes help in order to be liked rather than because you want to. Practise asking directly for what you need instead of hoping others will notice. People who care about you usually welcome the chance to give something back.
type2.high: The Helper pattern is strong in you. You are warm, generous and attentive to what others need, and you feel most valuable when you are helping. Your core fear is being unloved or unwanted. People experience you as caring and supportive. Tip: your own needs are just as legitimate as anyone else's, so name them openly. Help because you choose to, not to secure love. Growth comes when you let others care for you as well and trust that you are lovable without giving.

type3.name: Type 3: The Achiever
type3.short: Driven by the wish to succeed and be admired; fears being worthless or a failure.
type3.low: The Achiever pattern plays only a small role for you. Status, image and outward success are not your main drivers, and you do not measure your worth by what you accomplish. This gives you freedom from comparison. Tip: if you have goals you care about, a bit of ambition and visible progress can help you reach them. Let others see your achievements; modesty should not hide your strengths.
type3.mid: You recognise some Achiever traits. You like to do well and enjoy recognition, but your sense of worth does not depend entirely on success. You can work hard towards goals and still enjoy downtime. Tip: check whether the goals you pursue are truly yours or what others expect. Celebrate achievements, then also take time to enjoy life outside performance, with people who like you regardless of your results.
type3.high: The Achiever pattern is strong in you. You are ambitious, efficient and focused on success, and you know how to present yourself well. Your core fear is being worthless without your accomplishments. You motivate others and get things done. Tip: notice when you adapt your image to please others or work to avoid feeling empty. Spend time on activities with no goal at all. Growth comes when you value yourself for who you are, not for what you achieve.

type4.name: Type 4: The Individualist
type4.short: Driven by the wish to be unique and authentic; fears having no identity or significance.
type4.low: The Individualist pattern plays a minor role for you. You do not feel a strong need to be different or to explore every emotion in depth, and you are comfortable fitting in. This keeps you grounded and practical. Tip: make some room for self-expression, such as a creative hobby or honest conversations about feelings. Exploring what makes you unique can add richness to your life.
type4.mid: You recognise some Individualist traits. You value authenticity and have a rich inner life, but you do not feel fundamentally different from others. You can express emotions and still keep perspective. Tip: use your sensitivity creatively, for example through writing or art. When you feel misunderstood, check whether you have actually shared what you feel. Others often care more than you expect once they understand your inner world.
type4.high: The Individualist pattern is strong in you. You are sensitive, expressive and deeply in touch with your emotions, and you long to be authentic and understood. Your core fear is having no real identity or significance. You bring depth, creativity and honesty about feelings. Tip: notice when you focus on what is missing rather than what you have. Gratitude practices and practical routines can steady your moods. Growth comes when you realise that ordinary moments and connections can be meaningful too.

type5.name: Type 5: The Investigator
type5.short: Driven by the wish to understand and be competent; fears being helpless or overwhelmed.
type5.low: The Investigator pattern plays only a small role for you. You do not feel a strong need to withdraw and analyse before acting, and you share your time and energy easily. This makes you approachable and engaged. Tip: when facing complex decisions, give yourself some quiet research time before diving in. Deepening your knowledge in one area you care about can build confidence and expertise.
type5.mid: You recognise some Investigator traits. You enjoy learning and need some private time, but you can also engage actively with people and the world. You value knowledge without hiding behind it. Tip: notice when you pull back to observe instead of participating, especially in relationships. Sharing what you know, even before you feel fully ready, can be rewarding and often brings useful feedback and connection.
type5.high: The Investigator pattern is strong in you. You are curious, perceptive and independent, and you want to understand the world deeply. Your core fear is being helpless, incapable or drained by others' demands, so you guard your time and energy carefully. You bring insight and expertise. Tip: notice when gathering knowledge becomes a way to avoid action or feelings. Take small steps before you feel completely prepared. Growth comes when you trust that you have enough to engage fully with life and people.

type6.name: Type 6: The Loyalist
type6.short: Driven by the wish for security and support; fears being left without guidance or safety.
type6.low: The Loyalist pattern plays a minor role for you. You do not worry much about what could go wrong and feel secure without needing strong guidance or reassurance. This lets you act boldly. Tip: before big decisions, consciously consider possible risks or ask someone more cautious for their view. Loyalty and preparation can also be strengths worth developing, especially in teams that rely on you to think ahead.
type6.mid: You recognise some Loyalist traits. You value security and trusted relationships and can spot risks, but your doubts do not usually hold you back. You balance caution with confidence. Tip: when worry starts to grow, separate realistic risks from what-if scenarios. Trust your own judgement more often instead of looking for reassurance. Each time you act on it, your confidence in your own inner compass grows.
type6.high: The Loyalist pattern is strong in you. You are loyal, responsible and alert to risks, and you value trust and security highly. Your core fear is being without support or guidance in a dangerous world. You make a dependable team member who prepares for problems others overlook. Tip: notice when anxiety leads you to over-plan or doubt everyone, including yourself. Practise acting on your own judgement in small steps. Growth comes when you discover the inner security you have been seeking outside yourself.

type7.name: Type 7: The Enthusiast
type7.short: Driven by the wish for freedom and fun; fears being trapped in pain or deprivation.
type7.low: The Enthusiast pattern plays only a small role for you. You do not constantly seek new experiences and can stay with one thing, even when it is not exciting. This gives you focus and depth. Tip: allow yourself some spontaneity now and then, such as a short trip or a new hobby. A little playfulness can refresh your energy and relationships.
type7.mid: You recognise some Enthusiast traits. You enjoy fun, variety and new plans, but you can also commit and stay with difficult feelings. You balance optimism with realism and can enjoy both adventure and quiet. Tip: notice when you reach for distraction to avoid something uncomfortable. Finishing one project before starting the next will make your enthusiasm pay off and give you the deeper satisfaction of completion.
type7.high: The Enthusiast pattern is strong in you. You are optimistic, adventurous and full of ideas, and you love keeping your options open. Your core fear is being trapped in pain, boredom or limitation, so you often move quickly to the next exciting thing. You bring energy and joy wherever you go. Tip: practise staying with difficult emotions instead of escaping them. Choose a few commitments and see them through. Growth comes when you find satisfaction in depth, not only in variety.

type8.name: Type 8: The Challenger
type8.short: Driven by the wish to be strong and in control; fears being controlled or vulnerable.
type8.low: The Challenger pattern plays a minor role for you. You do not need to take control or prove your strength, and you rarely seek confrontation. This makes you easy to cooperate with. Tip: in situations where you or others are treated unfairly, practise speaking up firmly. Asserting yourself is not aggression; it is protecting what matters. Start with small situations, such as clearly stating a preference in a meeting.
type8.mid: You recognise some Challenger traits. You can be direct and protective and will take charge when needed, but you do not need to dominate. You show strength without losing sensitivity. Tip: notice when you push hard to avoid feeling vulnerable. Letting people see your softer side can deepen trust. Ask others how your directness lands; their answers may help you use your strength more wisely.
type8.high: The Challenger pattern is strong in you. You are confident, direct and protective, and you take charge naturally. Your core fear is being controlled, harmed or vulnerable, so you value strength and independence. You stand up for yourself and others and are not afraid of conflict. Tip: your intensity can overwhelm people, so lower your volume and listen fully before acting. Practise showing vulnerability with people you trust. Growth comes when you see that openness and gentleness are also forms of strength.

type9.name: Type 9: The Peacemaker
type9.short: Driven by the wish for inner and outer peace; fears conflict and disconnection.
type9.low: The Peacemaker pattern plays only a small role for you. You do not shy away from conflict and readily stand up for your own priorities. This keeps you active and clear about what you want. Tip: when tensions rise, practise listening to all sides before pushing your view. A calmer pace now and then can help you see the bigger picture.
type9.mid: You recognise some Peacemaker traits. You value harmony and can see different perspectives, but you also speak up when something matters to you. You balance calm with engagement. Tip: notice when you go along with others to avoid friction. Saying what you want, even in small things, keeps your relationships honest and prevents quiet resentment from building up. Your view adds something others cannot.
type9.high: The Peacemaker pattern is strong in you. You are calm, accepting and supportive, and you easily see every side of a situation. Your core fear is conflict, loss and disconnection, so you often smooth things over or set your own wishes aside. People feel at ease with you. Tip: notice when you go numb, procrastinate or merge with others' plans to keep the peace. Name your own priorities and act on them. Growth comes when you realise your voice matters and adds to harmony.

summary: You receive a score from 0 to 100 % for each of the nine Enneagram types; your highest score is shown as your main type. Most people recognise themselves in several types, so look at your top two or three as well. The Enneagram is a tool for self-reflection and growth, not a fixed label.
